title: CLIVE's live turns load no MCP server of the host's: only CLIVE's own tools
requested_outcome: The owner ruled on 8 October (DEC-071, ruling 26): "Never let your own MCP servers load into CLIVE's live turns?" — "Y". PR #103 (the persona bench) added a `strict_mcp_config` switch to MaxAgentSDKProvider (app/providers/max_agent_sdk.py), off by default and passed to the Agent SDK only when on, and turned it on for bench runs only. Turn it on for production: in app/runtime.py, the two MaxAgentSDKProvider(...) constructions (the owner's assistant around line 735 and the staff assistant factory around line 885) pass strict_mcp_config=True, so the claude CLI started for a live turn loads only the MCP servers CLIVE gives it (its in-process tools) and never the host user's own MCP servers or claude.ai connectors. Must not change: MaxAgentSDKProvider itself (its default stays False, and with False the options call still names nothing, byte for byte); app/bench/; the tools offered, their descriptions and schemas; the system prompt; allowed_tools and permission mode; anything about the API-key guard. Prove it in a new tests/test_strict_mcp_production.py: build the owner's and a staff assistant through app/runtime.py's own construction path with a fake SDK/options capture (no network, no CLI), and assert the options carry strict_mcp_config=True for both and that CLIVE's own MCP server is still present; assert a provider built directly with the default still omits it. Run every declared check yourself, exactly as declared, before reporting; report only a candidate on which all pass, or the base failure as it is.
acceptance_criteria: app/runtime.py's owner assistant and staff assistant MaxAgentSDKProvider constructions pass strict_mcp_config=True (tests).
A turn's Agent SDK options built through app/runtime.py carry strict_mcp_config=True and still include CLIVE's own in-process MCP server (tests).
MaxAgentSDKProvider's default is unchanged: built directly without the argument, its options do not name strict_mcp_config (tests).
No other file changes; tool descriptions, schemas and the system prompt are byte-identical (review: allowed_paths).
